tasks.description: Design and implement the database schema for storing problem details.

tasks.name: Develop Code Editor UI
tasks.description: Create the frontend interface for the code editor, including syntax highlighting and input/output sections.

tasks.name: Integrate Code Execution Backend
tasks.description: Develop the backend service to execute user-submitted code and return results.

tasks.name: Build Online Judge System
tasks.description: Implement the logic for evaluating code submissions against test cases.

tasks.name: Create User Profile UI
tasks.description: Design the frontend interface for user profiles, including stats and achievements.

tasks.name: Develop User Profile Backend
tasks.description: Implement the backend logic for managing user data and profile information.

tasks.name: Design Leaderboard UI
tasks.description: Create the frontend interface for displaying user rankings and scores.

tasks.name: Implement Leaderboard Backend
tasks.description: Develop the backend logic to calculate and serve leaderboard data.

tasks.name: Add Hints and Tutorials UI
tasks.description: Design the frontend interface for displaying hints and tutorials for problems.

tasks.name: Develop Hints and Tutorials Backend
tasks.description: Implement the backend logic to manage and serve hints and tutorials.

tasks.name: Test Problem Library Functionality
tasks.description: Perform testing to ensure the problem library works as expected.

tasks.name: Test Code Editor and Online Judge
tasks.description: Perform testing to ensure the code editor and online judge system function correctly.

tasks.name: Test User Profiles and Leaderboard
tasks.description: Perform testing to ensure user profiles and leaderboard features work as intended.

tasks.name: Test Hints and Tutorials
tasks.description: Perform testing to ensure hints and tutorials are displayed and managed correctly.

tasks.name: Deploy Problem-Solving Platform
tasks.description: Deploy the platform to a production environment.

T1.implementation_approach: Design a responsive UI using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript frameworks like React or Angular. Ensure intuitive navigation and filtering options.
T1.notes: Focus on user experience and accessibility.

T2.implementation_approach: Develop RESTful APIs using a backend framework like Node.js or Django to handle problem data operations.
data_structures: Relational database schema for problem data
T2.notes: Ensure secure and efficient API endpoints.

T3.implementation_approach: Design a relational database schema with tables for problems, categories, and tags. Use SQL or NoSQL databases.
T3.notes: Optimize for query performance and scalability.

T4.implementation_approach: Create a code editor using libraries like Monaco Editor or CodeMirror. Implement syntax highlighting and error detection.
T4.notes: Ensure compatibility with multiple programming languages.

T5.implementation_approach: Connect the code editor to a backend service for code execution using WebSocket or REST APIs.
T5.notes: Implement sandboxing for secure code execution.

T6.implementation_approach: Develop a system to evaluate code submissions using test cases. Use Docker for isolated execution environments.
T6.notes: Ensure scalability and security for concurrent submissions.

T7.implementation_approach: Design a user profile interface with sections for achievements, statistics, and settings.
T7.notes: Focus on personalization and ease of use.

T8.implementation_approach: Develop backend APIs to manage user profiles, including authentication and data updates.
data_structures: Relational database schema for user data
T8.notes: Ensure secure handling of sensitive user information.

T9.implementation_approach: Create a leaderboard interface with sorting and filtering options. Use charts for visual representation.

T10.implementation_approach: Develop backend APIs to fetch and update leaderboard data based on user performance.
data_structures: Relational database schema for leaderboard data
T10.notes: Implement caching for faster data retrieval.

T11.implementation_approach: Design an interface for hints and tutorials with multimedia support (videos, text, images).
T11.notes: Ensure content is easily accessible and well-organized.

T12.implementation_approach: Develop backend APIs to manage hints and tutorials, including content creation and updates.
data_structures: Relational database schema for tutorial content

T13.implementation_approach: Write unit and integration tests for the problem library using testing frameworks.

T14.implementation_approach: Test the code editor and online judge system for functionality, performance, and security.

T15.implementation_approach: Test user profiles and leaderboard features for correctness and scalability.
T15.notes: Focus on edge cases and concurrent usage.

T16.implementation_approach: Test hints and tutorials for accessibility and content correctness.

T17.implementation_approach: Deploy the platform using cloud services like AWS or Azure. Use CI/CD pipelines for automated deployment.
T17.notes: Ensure scalability and monitor performance post-deployment.

from flask_sqlalchemy import SQLAlchemy

# Initialize SQLAlchemy instance
db_instance = SQLAlchemy()

db = db_instance  # Direct SQLAlchemy instance

from app.database import db

class Problem(db.Model):
    __tablename__ = 'problems'

    id = db.Column(db.Integer, primary_key=True, autoincrement=True)
    title = db.Column(db.String(255), nullable=False)
    description = db.Column(db.Text, nullable=False)
    difficulty = db.Column(db.String(50), nullable=False)
    created_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, default=db.func.current_timestamp())
    updated_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, default=db.func.current_timestamp(), onupdate=db.func.current_timestamp())

    def __repr__(self):
        return f"<Problem {self.id}: {self.title}>"

from app.database import db

class User(db.Model):
    __tablename__ = 'users'

    id = db.Column(db.Integer, primary_key=True, autoincrement=True)
    username = db.Column(db.String(80), unique=True, nullable=False)
    email = db.Column(db.String(120), unique=True, nullable=False)
    password_hash = db.Column(db.String(128), nullable=False)
    created_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, default=db.func.now())
    updated_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, default=db.func.now(), onupdate=db.func.now())

    def __repr__(self):
        return f'<User {self.username}>'

from app.database import db

class Solution(db.Model):
    __tablename__ = 'solutions'

    id = db.Column(db.Integer, primary_key=True)
    problem_id = db.Column(db.Integer, db.ForeignKey('problems.id'), nullable=False)
    user_id = db.Column(db.Integer, db.ForeignKey('users.id'), nullable=False)
    code = db.Column(db.Text, nullable=False)
    language = db.Column(db.String(50), nullable=False)
    created_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, nullable=False, server_default=db.func.now())
    updated_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, nullable=False, server_default=db.func.now(), onupdate=db.func.now())

    problem = db.relationship('Problem', backref=db.backref('solutions', lazy=True))
    user = db.relationship('User', backref=db.backref('solutions', lazy=True))

from app.controllers.problem_controller import problem_blueprint
from app.controllers.user_controller import user_blueprint
from app.controllers.solution_controller import solution_blueprint

def register_blueprints(app):
    """
    Register all blueprints to the app instance.

    Args:
        app: The Flask application instance.
    """
    app.register_blueprint(problem_blueprint)
    app.register_blueprint(user_blueprint)
    app.register_blueprint(solution_blueprint)

from flask import Flask
from app.routes import register_blueprints
from app.database import db

def create_app():
    app = Flask(__name__)
    
    # Configure the app
    app.config['SQLALCHEMY_DATABASE_URI'] = 'sqlite:///app.db'
    app.config['SQLALCHEMY_TRACK_MODIFICATIONS'] = False
    
    # Initialize database
    db.init_app(app)
    
    # Register blueprints for routing
    register_blueprints(app)
    
    return app

from app import create_app

# Application entry point
app = create_app()

if __name__ == "__main__":
    app.run(debug=True)

# ACM Problem-Solving Platform

A website designed to help users solve ACM-style competitive programming problems.

## Features

- Problem Library: A comprehensive library of ACM-style problems categorized by difficulty and topic.
- Code Editor: An integrated code editor with support for multiple programming languages.
- Online Judge: An automated system to evaluate submitted solutions and provide real-time feedback.
- User Profiles: Profiles for users to track their progress, achievements, and rankings.
- Leaderboard: A leaderboard to display top-performing users and encourage competition.
- Hints and Tutorials: Hints and detailed tutorials for selected problems to help users learn.

## Setup

```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt
python app.py
```

## Usage

Open http://localhost:5000 in your browser.
